name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025)
licenseNote: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications is published by the OWASP Foundation under a Creative Commons licence. AEGIS references the entry identifiers only; every title and summary is original AEGIS wording describing the risk and is not the text of the list. Mapping an AEGIS record to an entry here is not a security assessment.
description: The ten most common security risks in applications built on large language models, as the OWASP community ranks them, with the AEGIS controls that address each for agents that take actions.

controls.title: Prompt injection
controls.summary: Instructions hidden in the content a model reads, or typed by a user, make it act outside its intended task; the application must detect, constrain and record such attempts.

controls.title: Sensitive information disclosure
controls.summary: A model reveals personal data, credentials or confidential business information in its outputs or in the calls it makes; data must be classified and masked, redacted or blocked before it leaves.

controls.title: Supply chain
controls.summary: Models, adapters, datasets, plugins and tools come from third parties whose provenance, licences and integrity must be checked and tracked.

controls.title: Data and model poisoning
controls.summary: Training, fine-tuning or retrieval data is manipulated to change a model's behaviour; sources and pipelines need controls and monitoring.

controls.title: Improper output handling
controls.summary: Model output is passed to other systems without validation, so injected content becomes code, queries or commands; outputs must be validated against a schema before use.

controls.title: Excessive agency
controls.summary: An agent is given more tools, permissions or autonomy than its task needs, so a mistake or an attack can cause real-world damage; grants should be minimal, actions gated and risky ones approved by a person.

controls.title: System prompt leakage
controls.summary: Secrets or sensitive logic placed in system prompts are exposed; prompts must not hold credentials and controls must not depend on the prompt staying hidden.

controls.title: Vector and embedding weaknesses
controls.summary: Retrieval stores and embeddings can be poisoned, leak data across tenants or be queried in ways that reveal content; access control and tenant separation apply to them too.

controls.title: Misinformation
controls.summary: Confident but wrong output is acted upon without verification; consequential decisions need human review and sources.

controls.title: Unbounded consumption
controls.summary: Unlimited requests, tokens or actions drive up cost or exhaust resources, including runaway agents repeating calls; rate limits, caps and monitoring are needed.
